transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get the batch-disposition huddle started for Batch H-418. As we all know, a cure-temperature alarm appeared during the Tuesday night run on Press 8, so we need to review everything before I make a final disposition decision on these 1,000 molded housings. I need two things from the group: first, the verbal laboratory report on the batch, and second, a pallet-level traceability check confirming the housings are staged on P1, P2, P3, and P4. Who has the lab results?

transcript.text: Elena, here's my verbal laboratory report on Batch H-418. After the cure-temperature alarm, I completed a differential-scanning-calorimetry review of retained samples. The results confirmed that exactly 240 of the 1,000 housings from Batch H-418 are undercured. These 240 undercured housings require a 4-hour thermal rework, and after rework, all 240 must undergo a hardness test before they can be released. I'll be uploading the full lab report to the quality system shortly.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Elena, here's the pallet-level traceability check you requested. I performed the pallet-level serial lookup after the alarm, and I can confirm that the 240 affected housings are exactly the 120 units on P2 and the 120 units on P3. P1 and P4 contain the 760 unaffected housings. I haven't attached the lookup to the batch record yet because we're still completing this disposition huddle, but I'll get that done right after we finish here.
transcript.speaker: A3
